basis: The printing heads this quaestio 'VERS. 19.' and it opens '(Vers. 19 et 20.) Et concepit adhuc Lia, et peperit filium sextum Jacob, et dixit Lia,'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Written at Bethlehem and named in Jerome's own De viris illustribus 135, finished in 393, among the works already published; the preface announces it as the first of a series of Hebrew Questions on the whole of Scripture that he never continued. The early 390s is as close as the evidence held here reaches. The date is the writing, not the 1845 printing and not Vallarsi's 1767 edition.
text: (Vers. 19 et 20.) Et concepit adhuc Lia, et peperit filium sextum Jacob, et dixit Lia, Dotavit me Deus dote bona: In hoc tempore habitabit mecum vir meus, quia peperi ei sex filios: et vocavit nomen ejus Zabulon. Ubi nos posuimus, habitabit mecum, et Septuaginta interpretati sunt, diliget me: in Hebraeo habet JEZBULENI (יזבלני). Et est sensus, quia sex filios genui Jacob, propterea jam secura sum: habitabit enim mecum vir meus. Unde et filius meus vocatur habitaculum. Male igitur et violenter in libro Nominum, Zabulon, fluxus noctis interpretatur.
